You are running HEADLESS. Never wait for input and never end your turn to wait for a notification: poll in loops instead. Hard time box: 80 minutes. Work fast but to a very high visual standard.

First run `entire session current` and stop if no session is shown or the id is f5117257-5211-42ae-823c-32aa228a28d9.

You are V-CAP, the capture session for the Heirloom demo video. Read ~/brief/VIDEO-BRIEF.md fully. Another session (V-MO) builds the Remotion motion design in `video/` at the same time.
- **You own `video/capture/`** (scripts, its own package.json, ASSETS.md, NOTES.md) and the output folders `~/video-out/captures/` and `~/video-out/broll/`. Don't touch other `video/` files.
- If the site needs a capture mode, you may make a minimal, query-param-guarded change in `site/web`. Then run `npm run build` (tests must pass), commit, and redeploy to Vercel production the same way as before (`cd site/web && vercel pull --yes --environment=production && vercel build --prod && vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod`), and check https://heirloom-proof.vercel.app returns 200.
- Before every push: `git pull --rebase`.

Milestones (commit and push your scripts after each; outputs stay out of git):
1. (≤10 min) Install ffmpeg (`sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg`). Set up `video/capture` with Playwright and Chromium (reuse the browsers already installed for site/web if possible). Build `capture.mjs`: a reusable frame-perfect capturer.
   - Uses Playwright's fake clock (`page.clock.install()` / `runFor(1000/60)`), eased scroll keyframes, an injected custom cursor (a bone dot with a brass ring) with eased moves and clicks, and JPEG frames → ffmpeg 60 fps CRF 14 yuv420p.
   - **Prove that virtual time drives Motion and three.js:** two frames 1 s apart must differ in the 3D hero. If not, switch to CDP virtual time.
   - Run the shots in parallel (up to 6 workers) to use the 8 cores.
2. (≤35 min) Site shots SH01–SH11 + SHM from the brief, against a local `vite preview` of main's current build (port 4400) or production. Encode each, then **Read 2–3 frames of every shot** (extract with ffmpeg). Fix jank, blank frames, half-loaded fonts or images, and wrong scroll framing.
3. (≤15 min) GitHub and web shots GH01–GH06, CFO01, EOL01:
   - dark colour scheme, 125% zoom, smooth eased scrolls, cookie banners hidden;
   - wait for fonts and network idle before frame 1.
   If cfo.ai doesn't render headless, record that and skip it.
4. (≤10 min) 3D beauty renders R3D01–R3D03 at 1920×1080, 60 fps, via virtual time (add a guarded `?shot=` camera path to the three demo if needed).
5. (≤10 min) Stock b-roll: 2–4 clips from Pexels or Mixkit only (macro mechanical watch movement or escapement ticking, brass gears), each ≥1080p.
   - Download the files directly (find the mp4 URLs on the clip pages).
   - Trim the best 6–10 s and colour-grade towards ink/brass (ffmpeg eq/curves, slight desaturation, crush blacks a little) → `~/video-out/broll/`.
   - Record the source page URL, author and licence for each in `video/capture/ASSETS.md`.
6. Write `~/video-out/captures/manifest.json` (id, file, seconds, fps, source, notes) and `video/capture/NOTES.md` (what you checked and fixed). Commit and push the scripts.

Rules:
- Real UI only; never fake the neatlogs UI.
- Never print .env values.
- Delete intermediate frame folders after encoding (disk has ~15 GB free).

Finish with the manifest contents, the total footage seconds, and any shot you couldn't get, with the reason.

# Heirloom demo video: production brief

**Goal:** a ≤2:50 product-launch-quality demo film for Heirloom (an agent that keeps end-of-life software patched). Viewers decide in the first 45 s.
- The owner supplies the voiceover (ElevenLabs), and possibly music and SFX, and does the final mix.
- We supply everything visual: real screen captures (frame-perfect), motion design, a picture-locked master timed to the script, per-scene clips, captions and an edit guide.

## Look and feel
- **Same world as the site** (https://heirloom-proof.vercel.app): "Proof instrument". Ink `#08090A`, raised `#0F1112`/`#16191B`, line `#23272A`, bone `#ECE6DA`, muted `#9A958A`, brass `#C8A86A`/`#E6CB8E`/`#8A6F3E`.
- **Verdict colours:** FIX READY `#5BC98F`, NOT AFFECTED `#7FB2FF`, UNPROVEN `#E8B44C`, AFFECTED `#FF6B5E`, NO PROBE `#8D8A83`.
- **Type:** Instrument Serif (display, italic accents), Geist (UI), Geist Mono (ids, hashes, terminal). The font files are in `site/web/public/fonts` or fontsource.
- **Motion language:** precise, confident, clockwork.
  - Eases `cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1)` (out) and `(0.65,0,0.35,1)` (in-out).
  - Springs `{damping: 200}` for UI, slightly bouncier `{damping: 18, stiffness: 120}` for stamps.
  - Kinetic type reveals word by word (y 24 px → 0, opacity, 40 ms stagger).
  - Guilloché lines draw on (stroke-dashoffset). Brass hairline underlines grow from the left.
  - Transitions: cuts on beat, a brass-ring iris or a gear-tooth wipe at act breaks.
- **No:** cheesy glitch, lens flares, purple, stock "hacker" footage, fake UI.
- Everything shown must be **real** (real site, real GitHub pages, real command output, real data from `site/web/public/site.json` and `evals/*.json`). Never fake the neatlogs UI: leave a labelled slot for the owner's recording.
- **Format:** 1920×1080, **60 fps**, H.264 High, yuv420p, Rec.709. Masters at CRF 14 (preset slow). A YouTube copy at about 16 Mbps. Silent renders; audio is optional (see Audio).

## Timeline (target 2:45; the VO is the spine; durations are re-timed to the real VO files when they arrive)
| # | Time | VO (exact text the owner will generate) | Visuals |
|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | 0:00–0:09 | "On the seventh of April, Django four-point-two reached end of life. No more security fixes." | Black → macro watch-movement b-roll (stock, or our 3D render), a single tick. Kinetic serif "7 April 2026" → "Django 4.2 · end of life", with a brass underline drawing. |
| S02 | 0:09–0:21 | "But Debian thirteen and Ubuntu twenty-four-oh-four still ship it. Since then, Django has published nineteen security advisories — and not one official patch for four-point-two." | Two engraved brass plates slide in: "Debian 13 · python-django 3:4.2.28-0+deb13u2" and "Ubuntu 24.04 · 3:4.2.11-1ubuntu1.18" (real strings). Then 19 real CVE ids cascade into a column, each getting a red "NO 4.2 PATCH" stamp, and the counter lands on "19 advisories · 0 upstream 4.2 patches". |
| S03 | 0:21–0:41 | "On October first, Ubuntu shipped a backport for one of them. Five days later, Django said its original fix was incomplete. We took Ubuntu's source package, ran a test calibrated on Django's own fix commits… and the code path Django closed is still reachable in Ubuntu's build." | Date plates "Oct 1 · Ubuntu ships its CVE-2026-15307 backport" and "Oct 6 · Django: CVE-2026-87890 amends that fix" lock around a glowing "5 days" band. Terminal (Geist Mono) shows the REAL probe run lines from the noble logs (FAIL ×3, `AssertionError: Lists differ: [<class 'bytes'>, <class 'bytes'>] != []`) → verdict chip AFFECTED → the claim sentence in serif: "noble's CVE-2026-15307 backport leaves the bytes path that upstream closed as CVE-2026-87890; our calibrated probe shows it." Small caption: "hand-written probe, calibrated on Django's fix commits dd0558d1^ / dd0558d1". |
| S04 | 0:41–0:52 | "That test was run by Heirloom — an agent that keeps end-of-life software patched, and proves which old versions are actually vulnerable." | Logo reveal: 3D brass movement (our render) turning. The hallmark seal stamps in; wordmark "Heirloom"; tagline "Old software, *kept honest.*" Cut to the site hero (capture). |
| S05 | 0:52–1:11 | "Its first rule: never trust a test that hasn't failed. For each advisory, Heirloom writes its own test, proves it fails on Django's vulnerable code and passes on the fix… and only then asks the real question: is the old version affected?" | Giant kinetic serif: "Never trust a test that hasn't failed." Then the **calibration triangle** motion graphic: U⁻ "upstream before fix" → 3 red FAIL lights; U⁺ "after fix" → 3 green PASS lights; then the line "Django 4.2.30" → verdict chip. Gates C1–C4 tick on. Cut to the site register → receipt certificate opening (capture). |
| S06 | 1:11–1:39 | "Then we let it run the whole campaign: nineteen advisories, replayed in the order Django published them. Thirteen candidate backports — each one failing before the fix, and passing after. Where it couldn't prove something, it filed the evidence instead of guessing. And when a new fix amended one it had already backported, it stacked the follow-up on its own pull request." | Site "Watch it work" capture: the bezel dial turning, tiles stamping in. Overlay lower-thirds: "13 candidate backports · FAIL×3 → PASS×3", "5 unproven → evidence filed, not guessed", "Oct 6 · stacked on its own backport · PR #21 on #20". A quick montage of the GitHub PR list (13 PRs) and PR #21's "Stacked on #20". |
| S07 | 1:39–1:56 | "Across the whole campaign, it asked me one question — a real judgement call about changing Django's behaviour. I answered once. It sealed the answer as a precedent, and the next case reused it without asking." | Site question-thread capture → GitHub issue #6 (the question + the owner's `/heirloom answer adopt-upstream-tests` comment) → the "PRECEDENT SEALED P001" stamp → PR #19 citing P001. |
| S08 | 1:56–2:19 | "We tested the method on cases with known answers. A naive pipeline once called a vulnerable version safe. Heirloom: zero times. Every claim in every pull request links to its neat-logs trace, and every backport links the Entire session of the agent that wrote it." | A backtest split motion graphic: "Naive pipeline: 1 false 'not affected'" (red) vs "Heirloom: 0" (green), with real numbers from evals/results.json. Then GitHub PR #13's claims table (capture) → **[SLOT: owner's neatlogs trace recording, 6 s]** → the PR commit's `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer (capture) → a terminal typing the real `entire checkpoint explain` output (from docs/entire/checkpoint-pr13-*.txt). |
| S09 | 2:19–2:30 | "Each advisory cost about twenty cents of model time. We modelled the business in C-F-O dot A-I: what that's worth to the teams who keep old software alive." | Count-up "$0.22 model cost per advisory (measured)" (from data) → site economics cards → the cfo.ai Base page (capture). |
| S10 | 2:30–2:45 | "Heirloom. Old software, kept honest. Every verdict is a test run you can open." | The site finale (the movement slowing to a stop) → end card: hallmark, "Heirloom", "heirloom-proof.vercel.app", "github.com/iamdflame/heirloom", "Built during #neatHack with neatlogs · Entire · cfo.ai". |

**Captions:** burned-in subtitles of the VO (Geist 34 px, bone on a 70% ink pill, bottom-centre, ≤42 chars per line), plus an `.srt`. Many viewers watch muted on X.

## Captures (session V-CAP): frame-perfect, 60 fps
- **Method (virtual time):** Playwright + Chromium, viewport 1920×1080. `page.clock.install()` before load; per frame, `page.clock.runFor(1000/60)`, set the scroll position, then screenshot (JPEG q=92) → `ffmpeg -framerate 60` → MP4 (CRF 14).
  - This gives perfectly smooth 60 fps even though the box renders WebGL slowly.
  - First verify that the fake clock drives Motion and three.js (two frames 1 s apart must differ). If it doesn't, use CDP `Emulation.setVirtualTimePolicy`.
  - Scroll with easing (in-out) between keyframe positions. Use a local `vite preview` of main's build with a `?capture=1` flag (disables Lenis and exposes `window.__scrollTo`) if needed. Also check that the result matches production.
- **Shots** (file names `~/video-out/captures/<ID>.mp4`):
  - **SH01** hero idle (3D movement turning), 8 s.
  - **SH02** hero → scroll to "Watch it work", 4 s.
  - **SH03** the full "Watch it work" campaign, 16 s (dial, stamps, the Oct 6 connector).
  - **SH04** finding section (plates lock, terminal FAIL×3), 9 s.
  - **SH05** register → a visible cursor moves to CVE-2026-6907 × Django 4.2.30 → click → receipt certificate with the calibration triangle animating, 10 s.
  - **SH06** method gear train, 8 s.
  - **SH07** question thread, 9 s.
  - **SH08** proof numbers, 6 s.
  - **SH09** economics, 6 s.
  - **SH10** evidence locker, 6 s.
  - **SH11** finale, 9 s.
  - **SHM** mobile 390×844 at DSF 3 scrolling the hero and campaign, 8 s.
- **Cursor:** render a tasteful custom cursor (a bone-coloured dot with a ring) injected into the page, moving on eased paths. No OS cursor.
- **GitHub** (dark colour scheme, logged out):
  - **GH01** PR #13: title, verdict table, then a smooth scroll to the claims table, 10 s.
  - **GH02** issue #6: the question → the owner's answer comment, 9 s.
  - **GH03** PR #19: the P001 citation, 6 s.
  - **GH04** PR #21: "Stacked on #20", 5 s.
  - **GH05** a backport commit page showing the `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer, 5 s.
  - **GH06** the fork's PR list (13 candidate backports), 5 s.
  - Hide cookie banners; zoom 125% so the text is legible in 1080p.
- **Other:** **CFO01** the cfo.ai Base Page (https://app.cfo.ai/s/25vRDQClPxqPWB5g), 8 s, if it renders headless. **EOL01** endoflife.date/django, 4 s.
- **3D beauty renders** (from the site's three demo, virtual time; a small `?shot=` camera-path param is fine):
  - **R3D01** a slow orbit around the movement, 10 s.
  - **R3D02** a macro dolly onto the "H" medallion, 6 s.
  - **R3D03** the gears speeding up, 5 s.
- **Stock b-roll:** 2–4 clips from **Pexels** (Pexels License) or **Mixkit** (Mixkit License) only. Macro mechanical watch movement or escapement ticking; brass gears turning. 1080p or higher. Record source URL and licence in `video/ASSETS.md`. Trim to the best 6–10 s and colour-match to ink/brass (ffmpeg `eq`/`curves`, slight desaturation).
- Write `~/video-out/captures/manifest.json` (id, file, duration, fps, source).

## Motion design and assembly (session V-MO): Remotion
- **Project:** `video/` in the heirloom repo (Remotion 4, TS, React). Renders are git-ignored; outputs go to `~/video-out/`.
- **Data:** import `site/web/public/site.json` (or `src/data/site.json`) and read evals for every number. Terminal lines come from real files: the noble 87890 probe logs on the `artifacts` branch (`git show artifacts:matrix/b4-20261011/CVE-2026-87890/...`), and `docs/entire/checkpoint-pr13-*.txt`.
- **Components:**
  - `KineticTitle`, `BrassUnderline`, `GuillocheRing` (procedural; reuse the site's generator), `Hallmark`;
  - `DistroPlates`, `CveCascade`, `DatePlates` (+ "5 days" band), `Terminal` (typed lines, a cursor);
  - `VerdictChip`, `CalibrationTriangle` (lights FAIL×3/PASS×3), `GateChecklist`;
  - `LowerThird`, `Counter` (count-up), `BacktestSplit`, `PrecedentSeal`;
  - `CaptureClip` (`OffthreadVideo` with a subtle push-in), `IrisTransition`, `EndCard`, `Captions` (from `timing.json`).
- **Composition `HeirloomDemo`** 1920×1080@60.
  - Scenes S01–S10 from `video/timing.json`: per scene, the start/duration in frames, the VO text and the caption chunks.
  - Default durations are the target times above. A script `video/scripts/retime.mjs` reads `video/public/audio/vo/S0x.mp3` with ffprobe when present, sets each scene to its VO length + padding (0.4 s head, 0.6 s tail; S10 holds the end card 4 s) and regenerates the captions.
- **Audio support (optional):**
  - if `video/public/audio/vo/S01.mp3…S10.mp3` exist, place them at the scene starts;
  - if `music.mp3` exists, lay it underneath at −18 dB with ducking to −24 dB under VO;
  - if `sfx/*.mp3` exist, place them on cue (tick, stamp, whoosh, boom).
  - Render `HeirloomDemo-silent.mp4` always, plus `HeirloomDemo-mix.mp4` when audio is present.
- **Deliverables** in `~/video-out/`:
  - `master/HeirloomDemo-silent.mp4` (+ `-captions.mp4` burned in) and `master/HeirloomDemo.srt`;
  - `scenes/S01.mp4…S10.mp4` (each scene alone, silent);
  - `captures/*` and `broll/*`;
  - `stills/*.png` (keyframes for review);
  - `EDIT-GUIDE.md`: per-scene timecodes, which VO file goes where, the SFX cue list with timecodes, music levels, export settings for YouTube (1080p60, H.264 16–20 Mbps, AAC 320 kbps), the neatlogs slot instructions.

## Quality bar (both sessions)
- Render stills at the key moment of every scene and **Read them**. Write the critique in `video/NOTES.md` and fix it before the final render.
- Watch for: legibility at 1080p (no text <28 px except mono ids ≥22 px), safe margins (5%), consistent brass and ink, no jank, no empty frames, no clipped words, captions in sync.
- **Honesty:**
  - only text from the VO table and real data;
  - "candidate backports"; no exploitability claim; the exact Ubuntu claim sentence;
  - the neatlogs UI never faked.
